routeSelection.basis: The normalized target merges current English Archaeology and Dutch Archeologie offerings. Their official curriculum pages show the same academic structure and compulsory sequence. The English trajectory is used as the representative pathway because the normalized display name is Archaeology and the English page provides the complete current component list; no content from the Dutch trajectory is added.

exception.reason: The UvA programme requires a cumulative archaeology curriculum: archaeological sources and theory, prehistoric-to-early-modern European archaeology, environmental, scientific and digital archaeology, artefact and material analysis, two credited field schools, excavation-to-publication training, heritage study and an archaeology thesis. UCR offers a small but valuable archaeology and heritage group, but it cannot sustain a complete 24-course archaeology-led programme without treating history, art history, media or general environmental and research-method courses as substitutes for missing archaeological practice and specialist method. A material-culture and ancient-societies direction fails because only three courses substantially teach archaeology. A heritage, museums and public-memory direction can form a coherent related humanities programme but would not be a defensible response to the target's fieldwork- and methods-centred academic identity. An environment, landscape and digital-analysis direction lacks archaeological survey, GIS, archaeometry, finds processing and excavation data. No candidate therefore passes the course-to-concept and coherence gates.

exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows in the current enriched UCR workbook, including outline-derived profiles, descriptions, topics, methods, prerequisites and Fall-2026-to-Spring-2029 availability. MCCHEAM112 Introduction to World Archaeology studies artefacts, manufacture, material culture and past communities; MCCHEAM213 Greek Archaeology studies early-democratic Greece; and MCCHEAM315 Heritage & Ancient Democracy connects ancient evidence with heritage and reception. MCCHEAM211, MCCHEAM312 and MCCHEAM316 contribute heritage, museums, curatorial practice and art-historical research, while MCCHEAM111 and MCCHEAM212 contribute broader art history. These courses support a genuine heritage or ancient-cultures direction, but do not supply archaeological stratigraphy, field recording, supervised excavation, archaeological survey, pottery/glass/metal analysis, materials identification, archaeometry, GIS or digital archaeology, environmental archaeology, or an archaeology research sequence. GOSHIST courses teach historical inquiry rather than archaeological method; MCCMEDI112 uses archaeology as a media-historical approach; environmental science and general qualitative or quantitative methods do not become archaeological field and laboratory training. The material-culture/ancient-societies, heritage/public-memory, and environment/landscape/digital-analysis candidates were each tested against the full catalogue. The first and third cannot support 23 substantively relevant non-PPD courses, while the second is a coherent neighbouring humanities programme but is too far from the comparator's defining disciplinary sequence to serve as its strongest complete UCR response.
